description: Figure 19 is a grouped bar chart comparing the average probing accuracy, measured as a percentage point difference, across four different MLP (multilayer perceptron) configurations for two models: mBERT (light blue bars) and XLM-R (dark blue bars). The horizontal axis lists the four MLP variations: “hidden:[50], linear”, “hidden:[1], linear”, “hidden:[100], ReLU”, and “hidden:[50, 50], ReLU”, indicating the size and activation function of the hidden layer(s). The vertical axis, labeled “% point difference”, ranges from –0.2 to +0.2, with tick marks at intervals of 0.1. For the first configuration (“hidden:[50], linear”), mBERT shows a negative difference of approximately –0.1, while XLM-R is slightly negative at around –0.05. In the second configuration (“hidden:[1], linear”), both models show positive differences, with mBERT at approximately +0.08 and XLM-R at +0.20. For the third (“hidden:[100], ReLU”), mBERT is negative at –0.08 and XLM-R is slightly positive at +0.03. In the final configuration (“hidden:[50, 50], ReLU”), mBERT is negative at –0.15 and XLM-R is negative at –0.10. The chart visually indicates that performance varies significantly by MLP architecture and model, with XLM-R outperforming mBERT in the second configuration and underperforming in the fourth.
